thread:
jen-cs: customer reported a sudden spike of 503s for hosted inference 16:02 UTC, multiple tenants affected, they saw ~15% error rate. Can eng take?
ryan-oncall: on it. I can already see a flurry of restarts in runner-ao cluster, pods restarting every ~90s. Attaching quick logs.
marta-sre: :eyes: looks like the containers are getting OOM/killed then k8s restarts them. saw CUDA OOM then a segfault in the runtime, crash loop.
deploy-bot: runner-ao-5 restarted at 2025-11-03T16:02:11Z (reason: OOMKilled)
ryan-oncall: snippet from /var/log/runners/runner-ao-5.log:
```
[16:01:59] ERROR runtime: cuda: out of memory while allocating 2147483648 bytes
[16:02:00] FATAL runtime: signal SIGSEGV (segfault) at 0x7f8a3d2a
[16:02:00] worker: aborting, core dumped
```
samir-ml: which model/version? large-context llama-70b-qlora:v3? We recently rolled a quant-swap for that pool yesterday.
ryan-oncall: yes, affected pool = hosted-llama-70b, model variant = llama-70b-qlora:v3, traffic spiked with long prompts (p95 context ~ 6k).
helena-eng: repro attempt: can we push a synthetic traffic spike and run with batch_size=16 and kv-prefetch enabled? that combo has regressed before.
marta-sre: we should avoid blasting prod. quick mitigation: flip routing to fallback variant (llama-70b-qlora:v2) and reduce max_batch_size at the routing policy to 8. will that impact latency?
ryan-oncall: good plan. I'm going to set an emergency routing override to fallback variant for the next 30m and patch runtime config to max_batch_size=8 for hosted-llama-70b.
ryan-oncall: commands I ran:
```bash
# reduce batch size in runtime config
redwoodctl config set --pool hosted-llama-70b --max-batch-size 8 --reason \"emergency OOM mitigation\"
# route traffic to v2
redwoodctl route set --model llama-70b-qlora:v2 --pool hosted-llama-70b --weight 100
```
jen-cs: please confirm once routing change is live so I can update customer.
deploy-bot: routing policy updated by ryan-oncall at 2025-11-03T16:06:41Z
ryan-oncall: change is live. error rate dropped to ~1.2% within 90s. p95 latency up ~40ms but stable.
samir-ml: looks like the qlora:v3 quant kernel has a bad path for very long sequences + certain seq packing that trips an allocation path (we have a failing unit test to add). I'll roll back the quant-swap candidate for the pool and run extended memtests.
marta-sre: rolling restart of runner-ao nodes in progress (drain + recreate) to clear bad allocator state. monitoring container restarts.
helena-eng: next steps: 1) reproduce with exact inputs customer provided (jen, can you attach sample?) 2) test quant-swap rollback and run 12h soak on staging with long context 3) add a hard cap per-request token allocation to avoid huge one-off allocations 4) update runbook with this mitigation.
jen-cs: attached sample prompt from customer in ticket #12345 — they hit 8k tokens in some sessions. I'll share the ticket link in PM.
ryan-oncall: follow-ups assigned: marta (node rolling restart + postmortem), samir (quant rollback + tests), helena (runbook + hotfix for allocation cap). I'll stay on watch for next 60m.
marta-sre: noted. creating incident page and will paste timeline.
jen-cs: I'll message customer that we've routed them to v2 and are working on a fix, ETA 6-8 hours for rollback + tests.
ryan-oncall: for now mitigation stands. if error rate creeps back up we'll fail traffic to managed fallback (cpu-backed) and engage customer account team.
helena-eng: quick note for postmortem: include exact kernel logs, memory map, and the sequence packing header (likely root cause).
jen-cs: thanks team :pray:
